newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus firms stall on scope of new entity - minister.
newsitem.headline: Airbus firms stall on scope of new entity - minister.

text.p: Partners in the European Airbus Industrie consortium have made progress in talks on changing its status to a joint stock company but problems persist on the scope of the new entity, the French transport minister said on Wednesday.

"There are problems which persist on the extent of the responsibilities and the scope of transfers from the industrial companies to the new entity," Bernard Pons told the lower house National Assembly at question time.
But he said there had been considerable progress as the Airbus chairman expects a general agreement by the end of 1996. pnt
Once the overall agreement is reached, it could take up to two years to adopt the new structure.
"It is clear that from the time the general agreement is reached, progress towards the definitive structure will require a year and a half to two years," Pons said.
Airbus partners are in discussions over the valuation and assets to be transferred to the new company, as well as what sort of firm it will be.
British Aerospace Plc (BAe) wants an Airbus with all the assets, skills and manufacturing facilities to be a large, integrated company.
France's SNI Aerospatiale wants the future Airbus to be major prime contractor, directing the work of subcontractors but having its own design office.

Further ahead, BAe envisages the new Airbus company as the eventual civilian wing of a pan-European aerospace grouping, which would also build military aircraft, built up from the present national companies.
Pons said it was clear that with last week's order for 120 Airbus A320 narrow-body planes from USAir and 16 A330s from the Emirates Gulf airline, Airbus was now leading the world market.

The USAir order represented a year's work for 10,000 workers, which gave a "beacon of hope" for workers at Aerospatiale's plant at Toulouse and elsewhere, whereas previously there had been worries about the future, Pons said.
Airbus wants to change to a joint stock company from the present cumbersome partnership structure to improve competitiveness and streamline decision-making.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
